value.rules_markdown:
- `src/` — single crate; one responsibility per module, core types in `types.rs`, each port is one trait in one file.
- `src/bin/tinysweeper.rs` — CLI; every subcommand declared even if milestone not landed.
- `presets/` — review policy as data (folder with `preset.toml`, `README.md`, optional prompt overrides).
- `vendor/tinyagents` — agent harness as git submodule; edit upstream, bump pin.
- `docs/modules/<module>/README.md` — one document per `src/` module.
- `examples/` — declared in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` so credential tests never build in CI.
- Rustfmt output, Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` modules/files, `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with `//!` module doc describing role and feature gating.
- Comments explain decision, not code; say why for load-bearing flags/orderings.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///` (becomes help text).
- Tests in-crate: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at bottom of module, move to sibling `test.rs` when large; no `tests/` directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock (`MockForge`) for test assertions.
- Lane behaviour covered by golden tests: fixture diff plus canned structured model response.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- The model never holds a write token; write credentials minted only in `src/apply/` after all model calls return.
- Contributor code is never executed; read diff/tree, do not build/run scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments, diffs are untrusted input; fence and label as data in prompts.
- Secrets found by scanners reported by type/location only; value never reaches comment, check-run summary, or log.
- Use concise imperative commit subjects; keep commits small, each coherent slice on its own.
- Pull requests state what changed, behaviour change, and how verified.
